items.suggested_title: Does homeowners insurance cover water damage? A Charleston homeowner's guide
items.notes: Highest-value decision-stage query in the seed family (1,900/mo, KD 10, $27 CPC). Lead with the sudden-and-accidental vs gradual-damage distinction, then the flood exclusion, which matters more in Charleston than almost anywhere: NFIP flood policies are separate and tidal/storm-surge flooding is never covered by a standard HO-3. Note that Paul Davis works directly with adjusters and documents moisture readings for the claim.

items.notes: Bridges the two highest-priority services in plan-input (water + mold). Lead with the 24-48 hour mold growth window and IICRC S520. items.suggested_title: How to fix water damage on a ceiling (and when the stain means something worse)
items.notes: KD 0 with 1,000/mo: the easiest ranking win in this run. Starts DIY-flavoured, so pivot hard on the triage test: a stain that spreads, sags, or reappears is saturated insulation and a moisture-meter job, not a paint job. Charleston angle: after a named storm, ceiling stains are usually wind-driven rain past the roof deck, which is a covered peril.
